title: C482/445/2014 of Pushpendra Nath Maliah AND OTHERS Vs Smt. Sujata Paul Maliah

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Crl. Misc. Application (C-482) No. 445 of 2014
Pushpendra Nath Maliah & others .......... Applicants

Versus
Smt. Sujata Paul Maliah ............. Respondent

Mr. L.K. Tiwari, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Lokendra Dobhal, Advocate for the complainant / respondent.
List of cases referred:
1. (2013) 3 SCC 330, Rajiv Thapar vs Madan Lal Kapoor
2. (2013) 1 SCC (Cri) 986, Amit Kapoor vs Ramesh Chander
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.

The applicants, by means of present
application / petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.,
seek to quash the entire proceedings of misc. case no.
76 of 2011, Sujata Paul vs. Pushpendra Nath Maliah
& others, under Sections 17, 18, 19 and 22 of
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act,
pending in the court of Judicial Magistrate I,
Dehradun, as also the order of issuing notice of
proceeding dated 20.06.2011 against the applicants.
2) Brief facts of the case are that the
respondent filed an application under Section 17, 18,
19 and 22 of the Protection of Women from Domestic
Violence Act against the applicants in the court of
Judicial Magistrate I, Dehradun, stating therein that
the respondent got married to Sri Sanjiv Maliah on
11.06.2004 at Dehradun. After marriage the
respondent lived with her husband at Dehradun till
15.02.2005 and thereafter at Calcutta and returned to

2
Dehradun on 15.04.2009. It is also averred that
property bearing no. 175/2/279, situated at Rajpur
Road, Dehradun is the joint property purchased by
Pushpendra Nath Maliah, Ballabh Das Maliah and
late Premendra Nath Maliah. Late Premendra Nath
Maliah was father-in-law of the respondent and
Pushpendra Nath Maliah and Ballabh Das Maliah are
her paternal father-in-laws. Late Premendra Nath
during his life time executed a perpetual lease deed of
his 1/3 share in the said property in favour of
husband of the respondent. It is alleged that the
applicants had an evil eye on the said 1/3 share
leased out to the husband of respondent and they
made every attempt to grab the said share and tried to
evict the respondent and her husband, who are living
in the said property and were in possession of five
rooms, kitchen, common drawing room, common open
land etc. In the night of 11.10.2009, applicant no. 4
Sanjay Maliah forcefully trespassed into the bedroom
of the respondent when she was alone and
intimidated her using criminal force. An FIR no.
72/09 u/s 354 IPC was registered at P.S. Rajpur
against applicant no. 4 in this regard. Applicants and
their family members through Jitender Prasad,
Sidheshwar Prasad and Mohan Prasad started making
mischief and causing unnecessary harassment to the
respondent and her husband. In such circumstances,
husband of the respondent was constrained to file a
civil suit bearing O.S. no. 265 of 2010, Sanjiv Mahiah
Vs Jitender Prasad and others, and succeeded in
obtaining permanent injunction against the
defendants restraining them permanently from
interfering in peaceful possession of the respondent in

3
the property aforesaid from the court of Civil Judge
(J.D.), Dehradun. Despite this, the applicants, their
family members and associates have not stopped
harassing the respondent. Again, on 28.11.2010,
when the respondent was cooking food, Jitender
Prasad and Sidheshwar Prasad entered the kitchen.
Applicant no. 2 also came there. She threatened,
abused and twisted the hand of the respondent. On
27.07.2010, at around 11:30 A.M., respondent found
the locks of two rooms broken. One necklace, a pair
of ear rings along with three pairs of apparels and
Rs.9500/- in cash was found stolen. Case crime no.
84/10 u/s 379, 380, 451 and 453 IPC was registered
against the accused persons on direction passed by
the court u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. The complainant /
respondent had also cited other instances when she
was harassed and threatened at the hands of the
applicants. Lastly it is averred that the applicants
tried their level best to evict the respondent and her
husband from the said property causing intervention
in private life of the respondent and her husband by
engaging security guards and put restrictions on them
in the house which is in their joint possession, thus
such acts comes under the purview of domestic
violence. Having heard learned counsel for the parties
on application filed by the respondent u/s 17, 18, 19
and 22 of Protection of Women from Domestic
Violence Act, learned Magistrate registered the same
on 20.06.2011 and issued notices to the applicants
through Protection Officer. Hence, present criminal
misc. application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.

4
3) At the very outset learned counsel for the
applicants would submit that the proceedings
initiated against the applicants is without any basis,
as the applicants do not fall within the meaning of
word 'respondent' as defined in the Domestic Violence
Act, 2005. It is contended that in fact the respondent
is trying to grab the said property as well as various
other family properties of the applicants on one
pretext or other. A civil suit no. 193/2011 was filed
by the applicants in the court of Civil Judge (Sr. Div.),
Dehradun and they succeeded in getting an ad
interim injunction against dispossession from the
respondent on 04.04.2011. It is further contended
that the respondent is not in possession of any room
in said property as alleged in her complaint. It is also
contended that filing of present complaint under
various provisions of Domestic Violence Act is nothing
but gross abuse of the process of law at the hand of
the respondent, who is not 'an aggrieved person' as
defined in Section 2(a) of the Act. Lastly it is argued
that every relative of the husband cannot be arrayed
as a respondent in the complaint till such time as the
complaint does not disclose what domestic
relationship the respondent shared with such relative
in the shared household.
4) Per contra, learned counsel for the
respondent would submit that the respondent is
legally wedded wife of Sri Sanjiv Maliah. It is
contended that the property in question was
purchased jointly and construction over the same has
also been done jointly. In fact, father-in-law of the
respondent used to stay at the said property and used

5
to look after his business at Dehradun and the
applicant nos. 1 and 5 used to stay at West Bengal. It
is also contended that the respondent is resident in
the said property since April 2009 and there is only
one kitchen where food is cooked jointly. It is argued
that the aforesaid misc. case is filed in respect to the
domestic violence committed by the applicants with
the respondent while her stay at the said property as
a shared household and whatever rights have been
claimed is being claimed as the respondent is legally
wedded wife of Sri Sanjiv Maliah having 1/3 undivided
share in the said property. In reply to the fact that
the respondent is not an 'aggrieved person' it is stated
that the respondent is an aggrieved person as defined
u/s 2(a) of the Domestic Violence Act, as she is living
in a domestic relation being related to the applicants
by consanguinity, marriage and a family member
living together as a joint family is being subjected to
domestic violence in order to throw her out from the
said property. Lastly it is submitted that from a bare
perusal of the contents of the application and affidavit
u/s 23(2) of Domestic Violence Act the respondent
had every right to exercise her legal rights.
5) Perusal of the documents brought on
record would reveal that the trial court on receipt of
the said application rejected the interim relief
application vide its order dated 27.01.2014. By
impugned order dated 20.06.2011, the trial court has
registered the misc. case filed u/s 17, 18, 19 and 22
of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence
Act and sought report from the Protection Officer by

6
23.06.2011 and notices were issued to the opposite
parties (applicants herein).
6) Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the material brought on record.
7) Impugned order dated 27.01.2014 is an
interlocutory order and by the order impugned only a
report has been sought from the Protection Officer
and notices were issued to the applicants.
8) A detailed counter affidavit has been filed
by the respondent. The averments made in the
counter affidavit were not denied by the applicants by
way of filing rejoinder affidavit.
9) Having heard learned counsel for the
parties and on careful perusal of the documents
brought on record, this Court is of the considered view
that whether, the applicants are innocent or not, is
required to be seen by the trial court, after recording
the evidence of the witnesses. It is not just and
proper on the part of this Court to come to the
conclusion that the applicants are innocent with half
baked evidence before it, at this stage.
10) Hon'ble Apex Court in Amit Kapoor vs.
Ramesh Chander and another2 has laid down
certain principles in respect of exercise of jurisdiction
under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. One of the principle is
that the Court should apply the test as to whether the
uncontroverted allegations, as made from the record
of the case and the documents submitted therewith,

7
prima facie establish the offence or not. If the
allegations are so patently absurd and inherently
improbable that no prudent person can ever reach
such a conclusion and where the basic ingredients of
a criminal offence are not satisfied then the court may
interfere. Where the factual foundation for an offence
has been laid down, the courts should be reluctant
and should not hasten to quash the proceedings even
on the premise that one or two ingredients have not
been stated or do not appear to be satisfied if there is
substantial compliance with the requirements of the
offence. The power is to be exercised ex debito
justitiae, i.e., to do real and substantial justice for
administration of which alone, the courts exists.
11) The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rajiv
Thapar and others vs. Madan Lal Kapoor1 has
held as under:-
"28. The High Court, in exercise of its
jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.,
must make a just and rightful choice. This is
not a stage of evaluating the truthfulness or
otherwise of allegations levelled by the
prosecution/complainant against the
accused. Likewise, it is not a stage for
determining how weighty the defences
raised on behalf of the accused is. Even if
the accused is successful in showing some
suspicion or doubt, in the allegations levelled
by the prosecution/ complainant, it would be
impermissible to discharge the accused
before trial. This is so, because it would
result in giving finality to the accusations
levelled by the prosecution/ complainant,
without allowing the prosecution or the
complainant to adduce evidence to
substantiate the same. The converse is,
however, not true, because even if trial is
proceeded with, the accused is not subjected
to any irreparable consequences. The

8
accused would still be in a position to
succeed, by establishing his defences by
producing evidence in accordance with law.
There is an endless list of judgments
rendered by this Court declaring the legal
position, that in a case where the
prosecution/complainant has levelled
allegations bringing out all ingredients of the
charge(s) levelled, and have placed material
before the Court, prima facie evidencing the
truthfulness of the allegations levelled, trial
must be held."
12) In view of the above, in exercise of
jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., this Court
does not find any ground to interfere in quashing the
proceedings of misc. case no. 76 of 2011, Sujata Paul
Maliah Vs Pushpendra Nath Maliah, pending against
the applicants under Sections 17, 18, 19 and 22 of
the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act,
2005.
13) The present Criminal Miscellaneous
Application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is devoid of
merit and is accordingly dismissed. Interim order, if
any, stands vacated.
14) Court concerned be informed accordingly.
